effect_mechanism: Groundwater recharge now counts as a component of catchment water yield, so this row holds two kinds of evidence. Most units report recharge and rising water tables at or near capture structures: the proportion of runoff infiltrated through check dams can reach more than 50%, with recharge linked to episodic storm events [ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_luca21_1]; groundwater tables rise in the vicinity of filled check dams, and sand dams can raise the local groundwater [ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_fran21_1, ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_ritc21_1]; in India additional recharge from check dams and other water harvesting structures was estimated at 480 million cubic meters per annum, groundwater levels rose in 16 of 21 non-desert districts with an average increase of 1.42 meters, and a state survey found levels increased in 22 of the 31 districts [ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_verm19_1, ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_verm19_3, ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_verm19_2]; the Uttarakhand water budget shows aquifer recharge up 3.3 percent and water yield from catchment areas up 4.9 percent [ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_utk22_5], and ISRO survey data record increased recharge in treated areas [ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_iegind11_3]; terraces would cause a groundwater recharge of 15 to 25% of rainfall, and modelling of contour ridges in Morocco estimates a 50% increase in recharge [ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_roose06_1, ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_willem21_1]; stone bunds, zaï and half-moons applied at watershed scale increase ground water level, and in Burkina Faso improved well levels are linked to SWC measures that control surface runoff and improve infiltration [ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_zoug14_1, ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_kabo04_1]; communities in Mauritania, spate beneficiaries in Yemen and an Ethiopian public-works assessment report rising well levels, increased groundwater or water-table improvements [ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_mrt14_1, ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_yem12_1, ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_yem12_2, ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_eth16_7]; justification.conditionality: This row is for downstream users and basin planners: it asks what capturing water upstream does to the water that reaches streams and reservoirs below, not whether the farm that captures it has more. Against the recharge reports, the downstream streamflow impacts of small-scale water storage systems have in other cases been limited, even when implemented widely [ev_water_yield_rock10_1]. The recharge gains have limits in their own sources: without data from untreated sites the Indian project impact is unclear [ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_iegind11_3], subsidised tube-well pumping has possibly wiped out any increases in recharge [ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_iegind11_4], and in Burkina Faso the number of wells with water year round has not increased significantly [ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_kabo04_2]. The Uttarakhand figures are a modelled water budget [ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_utk22_5], and most other units are programme reports or cited statements; no unit compares downstream flow with and without catchment treatment. The digues filtrantes finding is cited from another study, with no figures [ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_sawa11h1_6].

effect_mechanism: In the Maghreb, mechanised bund systems, built with large machines that scrape a 4 to 10 m strip to raise bunds 1.5 to 2 m high every 30 to 50 m, considerably reduce the water collected in downstream hill reservoirs and cost 10 to 25% of the cultivable area [ev_water_yield_roos10_1]. On the other side, earth and stone bunds in Mauritania were built to facilitate water infiltration and replenish groundwater tables, and surveyed communities expressed satisfaction with the rising levels of water in their wells [ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_mrt14_1]; in the Peruvian Andes a few studies have observed catchment-level changes such as increased aquifer recharge, which the source calls plausible but not generalisable [ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_locat20_1].
conditionality: This row is for downstream users and basin planners: it asks what capturing water upstream does to the water that reaches streams and reservoirs below, not whether the farm that captures it has more. The sides are measured in different places: the gains are well levels and recharge around the treated land, the loss is water reaching downstream hill reservoirs below mechanised bunds, and a downstream loss can coexist with the local gain. The source ties the loss to mechanised construction and cites it from earlier work in an expert manual; the Mauritanian gain is a lender-reported community perception for works that also included fencing [ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_mrt14_1]; and in the Peruvian Andes trenches had little effect on increasing baseflow, with hydrogeological characteristics key to explaining their impact [ev_water_regulation_locat20_1]. No finding is quantified.

effect_mechanism: Check dams and sand dams recharge local groundwater: the proportion of runoff infiltrated through check dams can reach more than 50%, with recharge linked to episodic storm events [ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_luca21_1]; groundwater tables rise in the vicinity of filled check dams [ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_fran21_1]; sand dams can raise the local groundwater [ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_ritc21_1]; in India additional recharge from check dams and other water harvesting structures was estimated at 480 million cubic meters per annum, contributing to post-monsoon stabilization of groundwater levels, and a state survey found groundwater levels increased in 22 of the 31 districts [ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_verm19_1, ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_verm19_2]; and a review lists aquifer recharge among benefits cited for water harvesting [ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_saru19_1]. On the other side, on China's Loess Plateau, a large campaign of check-dam construction carried out since the 1970s to retain floodwater and intercept soil sediments reduced streamflow by approximately 39% [ev_water_yield_luca21_1]. Embrapa says its barraginhas in Brazil help recharge groundwater by raising the water table and revitalise springs and rivers [ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_mira19_6].
conditionality: This row is for downstream users and basin planners: it asks what capturing water upstream does to the water that reaches streams and reservoirs below, not whether the farm that captures it has more. Both sides involve check dams but measure different things: recharge and water tables at or near the structures, against streamflow below a campaign of check dams built at very large scale to retain floodwater. The gain is local and the sand-dam effect is often limited in space and time [ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_ritc21_1]. Every unit is a secondary citation in a review or report, the Indian recharge figure is an estimate [ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_verm19_1], and the 39% is a figure the review cites from another study [ev_water_yield_luca21_1]; no unit compares downstream flow with and without the works. The barraginha recharge statement is Embrapa's self-assessment of its own technology, with no measurement behind it [ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_mira19_6].

The Cameroonian figure is a conditional estimate and the Moroccan figure a modelling result, both cited secondarily [ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_roose06_1, ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_willem21_1]. The Cameroonian source flags that the drainage could reach the unterraced piedmonts, a much more fragile environment [ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_roose06_1]. On-slope supply evidence for terraces is in the terracing water stress row.

effect_mechanism: In semi-arid Brazil, water from runoff-harvesting ponds applied as supplemental irrigation during in-season dry spells has reduced crop-loss risk in years of irregular rainfall, and water stored in production cisterns can reduce livestock mortality in severe droughts [ev_drought_hazard_brito07_10, ev_drought_hazard_castro22_2]. A Burkina Faso review concludes that soil and water conservation techniques helped reduce vulnerability to drought and famine [ev_drought_hazard_sawa11h1_7].
conditionality: Against this, subsurface dams tended to dry out in a rainless year and small ones do not withstand long dry spells; these units record no benefit when storage is exhausted, a shortfall rather than damage [ev_drought_hazard_cirilo03_2, ev_drought_hazard_cirilo03_3]. All units come from Brazilian research and programme authors, an upper-middle-income context adjacent to the target, and none gives a drought-impact metric. That Burkina Faso conclusion is the author's overall judgement, with no measured drought-year contrast behind it [ev_drought_hazard_sawa11h1_7].

effect_mechanism: The evidence from mixed crop-livestock farms is thin and all points the same way: in an Ethiopian Rift Valley maize trial the plots without mulch were the ones particularly affected by the season's dry spells [ev_drought_hazard_sime15h2_1], and in Brazil Embrapa describes its barraginhas, small semicircular runoff-retention basins dug along runoff paths in pastures and croplands, as storing water in the soil by infiltration and easing the effects of droughts on crops in the lowlands [ev_drought_hazard_mira19_8].
conditionality: Neither unit measures a drought-year contrast or says how large the effect is. The Ethiopian finding is a field observation of which plots wilted during mild dry spells, not a tested yield contrast, and says nothing about a severe drought [ev_drought_hazard_sime15h2_1]. The barraginha statement is Embrapa's self-assessment of its own technology, with no normal-year reference, and comes from an upper-middle-income Brazilian setting rather than the East African semi-arid zone this row is scoped to [ev_drought_hazard_mira19_8].

effect_mechanism: Across mixed soil and water conservation and water-harvesting programmes, the reported route to lower food insecurity is higher yields and irrigated gardens. A review tabulates significantly increased food security from check dams and infiltration pits in Malawi [ev_food_security_ngur26_1]; Brazilian studies judge production-cistern irrigation of small beds feasible and important for household food security [ev_food_security_castro22_3]; and higher yields are cited as improving food security in Burkina Faso, especially on farms with soil and water conservation on over half of their plots [ev_food_security_sawa11h1_5].
conditionality: The gain is only slight because the supporting findings are qualitative, cited second-hand and give no size, while the independent evaluations point the other way. In Ethiopia, an impact evaluation of a bundled watershed project found no significant food-security effect for treated households at any participation level [ev_food_security_abate21_4], and public-works participation in communal soil and water investments did not translate into increased food security, possibly because of the short programme [ev_food_security_arega24_1]; both concern mostly off-farm community works. In Niger, families with soil and water conservation produced a surplus of 70 percent in good rainfall years but a deficit of 28 percent in low-rainfall years [ev_food_security_kabo04_1], so benefits may not hold in the dry years that matter most.

effect_mechanism: In the tropical highlands, soil and water conservation has measured yield gains and measured yield losses, depending on the practice. Gains: an Ethiopian synthesis finds mean grain-yield gains of 322 kg per hectare for stone bunds, 554.3 for tied ridges and 629.2 for mulching, stone and soil bunds raising yields by up to 10% in Tigray, and stone bunds raising soil total nitrogen from 0.16 to 0.20% [ev_crop_yield_adim16_1, ev_crop_yield_adim16_3, ev_crop_yield_adim16_4, ev_crop_yield_adim16_8, ev_soil_nitrogen_adim16_1]; in a Kenyan highland trial, tied ridges in long rains with dry spells gave 4.10 against 3.15 t of maize per hectare with manure and fertiliser, and 2.53 against 1.82 t without inputs (not significant), and tended to give less variable yields [ev_crop_yield_ndun23_3, ev_crop_yield_ndun23_1, ev_yield_stability_ndun23_1]; in Peru, 2 to 4-year old bench terraces gave 20% greater yields than adjacent sloping fields [ev_crop_yield_wei16_4]. Losses: in the same Ethiopian synthesis fanya juu and soil bunds were associated with yield losses of 54 to 193 kg per hectare, bunds cut yields by up to 7% in the first few years, and annual rainfall above 1000 mm affected performance negatively, which the authors suggest may be waterlogging in the furrows of structures [ev_crop_yield_adim16_2, ev_crop_yield_adim16_7, ev_crop_yield_adim16_6].
conditionality: The class is set by the gains. The fanya juu and soil bund losses and the finding that annual rainfall above 1000 mm affected performance negatively are held out of it, because the synthesis puts that effect down to excessive water availability (water logging) on the furrows of structures [ev_crop_yield_adim16_2, ev_crop_yield_adim16_6]: they are logged as a performance caveat — these structures should not be applied where rainfall is that heavy — rather than as production evidence. The evidence points to three things that separate gains from losses. Practice type: stone bunds, tied ridges and mulching gained, while graded and level fanya juu, soil bunds and grass strips lost yield in the Ethiopian table [ev_crop_yield_adim16_3, ev_crop_yield_adim16_2]. Rainfall: the gaining practices were studied at lower average rainfall (695.1 mm for tied ridges, 876.7 mm for mulching) than the losing bunds (1030.2 to 1454.3 mm), and rainfall above 1000 mm reduced performance [ev_crop_yield_adim16_3, ev_crop_yield_adim16_6]; practice and rainfall travel together in that table, so the two cannot be fully separated. Time: bunds lose yield in the first few years [ev_crop_yield_adim16_7]. For a Task Team Leader the actionable reading is to match the structure to the rainfall regime, favouring in-field moisture capture in drier highlands and avoiding fanya juu and soil bunds where waterlogging is likely, and to budget for an early yield dip. At the dry end, tied ridging gave no advantage in the Kenyan short rains with meteorological droughts, since there was little rain to hold [ev_crop_yield_ndun23_2, ev_crop_yield_ndun23_4, ev_crop_yield_ndun23_5]. On quality, both sides rest mainly on the same Ethiopian synthesis of unweighted means pooled across studies; the Kenyan result is a single-site trial whose lower-variability finding was not tested, and the Peruvian figure is cited in a review [ev_crop_yield_adim16_1, ev_yield_stability_ndun23_1, ev_crop_yield_wei16_4].

effect_mechanism: Soil and water conservation and water harvesting have been found both to raise and to lower production. Gains come from retaining moisture and soil: a meta-analysis of traditional in-situ water harvesting finds a pooled yield gain of 71% over controls, with 69% for soil and stone bunds and gains of 71.7% for maize and 68.2% for sorghum without fertiliser [ev_crop_yield_tefe24_1, ev_crop_yield_tefe24_4, ev_crop_yield_tefe24_7, ev_crop_yield_tefe24_8]; four studies in a systematic review find 20–24 per cent gains in crop yield or value of production, particularly in regions with low rainfall or high climatic variability [ev_crop_yield_mala24_1, ev_crop_yield_mala24_3, ev_crop_yield_mala24_5]; zai pits combined with stone lines in Burkina Faso are reported to raise sorghum yields by over 100% [ev_crop_yield_ngur26_3]; Ethiopian early adopters had a 15.2 percent higher value of production and invested plots 20.6 percent higher [ev_agricultural_production_value_schmidt12_1, ev_agricultural_production_value_schmidt12_4]; physical structures buffered crop growth against the 2015 severe drought in Ethiopia [ev_crop_yield_meaza22_1]; and dry spells can be bridged through water management [ev_crop_yield_rock10_1]. Programme reports add rainfed yield gains of 24% to 26% in Karnataka and 20.8% in Uttarakhand, yields rising from 0.5 to more than 1.2 t per hectare in wetter Mauritanian watersheds, and crop diversification from water harvesting with irrigation [ev_crop_yield_iegind11_1, ev_crop_yield_utk22_1, ev_crop_yield_mrt14_2, ev_agricultural_production_value_arega24_2]. Losses come from structures taking cropland and from excess water: in an Ethiopian synthesis fanya juu and soil bunds were associated with yield losses of 54 to 193 kg per hectare, bunds cut yields by up to 7% in the first few years, and rainfall above 1000 mm affected performance negatively, possibly through waterlogging [ev_crop_yield_adim16_2, ev_crop_yield_adim16_7, ev_crop_yield_adim16_6]; plots with bunds yielded less than non-conserved plots in high-rainfall western Amhara [ev_crop_yield_schmidt12_10]. A review cites soil and water conservation structures combined with biological measures raising wheat production by 30–45% over business-as-usual [ev_crop_yield_tade23h1_2]. Soils on Burkina Faso farms using soil and water conservation techniques had higher nitrogen contents than the control farm, used here as a component [ev_soil_nitrogen_sawa11h1_4]. The water-productivity evidence points the same way: FAO compilers list improved water use efficiency among the main benefits of rainwater harvesting, the WOCAT guideline authors find that all water harvesting groups indicate improved water use efficiency, mostly high to medium, through reduced evaporation loss and better soil water availability, and a review sentence, citing earlier work, says capture approaches often lead also to higher water productivity because denser canopies shade the soil [ev_rain_water_productivity_faoslm11_1, ev_rain_water_productivity_wocwh13_1, ev_rain_water_productivity_rock10_1].
conditionality: The class is set by the gains. The excess-water losses are held out of it as a caveat on where the practice performs rather than as production evidence: annual rainfall above 1000 mm affected performance negatively, which the synthesis puts down to water logging on the furrows of structures, fanya juu and soil bunds were associated with yield losses of 54 to 193 kg per hectare, and plots with bunds yielded less than non-conserved plots in high-rainfall western Amhara [ev_crop_yield_adim16_6, ev_crop_yield_adim16_2, ev_crop_yield_schmidt12_10]. Bunds should not be applied where rainfall is that heavy. The evidence itself names what separates gains from losses. Rainfall: gains concentrate in low-rainfall or variable areas and in drier periods, while bunds lose yield in high-rainfall areas, and in Tigray bunds slightly raised productivity in drier periods but reduced it in moist seasons because cropped area was lost to the bunds [ev_crop_yield_mala24_3, ev_crop_yield_schmidt12_10, ev_crop_yield_schmidt12_8, ev_crop_yield_adim16_6]. Time and maintenance: value of production rose only after structures had been maintained for at least 7 years, later adopters saw no significant gain, and bunds cut yields in the first few years [ev_agricultural_production_value_schmidt12_5, ev_agricultural_production_value_schmidt12_2, ev_crop_yield_adim16_7]. Who decides: imposed structures often reduced cultivable area by 3 to 20% without improving productivity, and structures promoted mostly off-farm for community resource protection gave no gain [ev_crop_yield_roose94_5, ev_crop_yield_abate21_1]. Severity: dry spells can be bridged but yields cannot be sustained in a meteorological drought [ev_crop_yield_rock10_2]. Practice: fanya juu and soil bunds account for the measured losses [ev_crop_yield_adim16_2]. The actionable distinctions are therefore siting by rainfall regime, farmer-owned rather than imposed structures, and a maintenance horizon of years. On quality, many of the largest gains are from bundled programmes or lender completion reports (Ethiopia public works, India watershed projects, Mauritania), with value of production and forage biomass used as proxies, while the losses come from an Ethiopian synthesis and a matched study; the drought finding is a secondary citation in a review [ev_crop_yield_utk22_1, ev_crop_yield_mrt14_2, ev_forage_productivity_mrt14_3, ev_crop_yield_meaza22_1]. The wheat figure is a review's citation of a package that includes biological measures [ev_crop_yield_tade23h1_2]. The nitrogen finding is a content on farm soils, not a yield [ev_soil_nitrogen_sawa11h1_4]. These are compiler and author judgements across groups, direction only, and the review sentence is second-hand; the WOCAT authors also note that some case studies indicate little to no improvement in water use efficiency [ev_rain_water_productivity_faoslm11_1, ev_rain_water_productivity_wocwh13_1, ev_rain_water_productivity_rock10_1].

justification.mechanism: Soil and water conservation and water harvesting have been found both to raise and to lower production. Gains come from retaining moisture and soil: a meta-analysis of traditional in-situ water harvesting finds a pooled yield gain of 71% over controls, with 69% for soil and stone bunds and gains of 71.7% for maize and 68.2% for sorghum without fertiliser [ev_crop_yield_tefe24_1, ev_crop_yield_tefe24_4, ev_crop_yield_tefe24_7, ev_crop_yield_tefe24_8]; four studies in a systematic review find 20–24 per cent gains in crop yield or value of production, particularly in regions with low rainfall or high climatic variability [ev_crop_yield_mala24_1, ev_crop_yield_mala24_3, ev_crop_yield_mala24_5]; zai pits combined with stone lines in Burkina Faso are reported to raise sorghum yields by over 100% [ev_crop_yield_ngur26_3]; Ethiopian early adopters had a 15.2 percent higher value of production and invested plots 20.6 percent higher [ev_agricultural_production_value_schmidt12_1, ev_agricultural_production_value_schmidt12_4]; physical structures buffered crop growth against the 2015 severe drought in Ethiopia [ev_crop_yield_meaza22_1]; and dry spells can be bridged through water management [ev_crop_yield_rock10_1]. Programme reports add rainfed yield gains of 24% to 26% in Karnataka and 20.8% in Uttarakhand, yields rising from 0.5 to more than 1.2 t per hectare in wetter Mauritanian watersheds, and crop diversification from water harvesting with irrigation [ev_crop_yield_iegind11_1, ev_crop_yield_utk22_1, ev_crop_yield_mrt14_2, ev_agricultural_production_value_arega24_2]. Losses come from structures taking cropland and from excess water: in an Ethiopian synthesis fanya juu and soil bunds were associated with yield losses of 54 to 193 kg per hectare, bunds cut yields by up to 7% in the first few years, and rainfall above 1000 mm affected performance negatively, possibly through waterlogging [ev_crop_yield_adim16_2, ev_crop_yield_adim16_7, ev_crop_yield_adim16_6]; plots with bunds yielded less than non-conserved plots in high-rainfall western Amhara [ev_crop_yield_schmidt12_10]. A review cites soil and water conservation structures combined with biological measures raising wheat production by 30–45% over business-as-usual [ev_crop_yield_tade23h1_2]. Soils on Burkina Faso farms using soil and water conservation techniques had higher nitrogen contents than the control farm, used here as a component [ev_soil_nitrogen_sawa11h1_4]. The water-productivity evidence points the same way: FAO compilers list improved water use efficiency among the main benefits of rainwater harvesting, the WOCAT guideline authors find that all water harvesting groups indicate improved water use efficiency, mostly high to medium, through reduced evaporation loss and better soil water availability, and a review sentence, citing earlier work, says capture approaches often lead also to higher water productivity because denser canopies shade the soil [ev_rain_water_productivity_faoslm11_1, ev_rain_water_productivity_wocwh13_1, ev_rain_water_productivity_rock10_1].
justification.conditionality: The class is set by the gains. The excess-water losses are held out of it as a caveat on where the practice performs rather than as production evidence: annual rainfall above 1000 mm affected performance negatively, which the synthesis puts down to water logging on the furrows of structures, fanya juu and soil bunds were associated with yield losses of 54 to 193 kg per hectare, and plots with bunds yielded less than non-conserved plots in high-rainfall western Amhara [ev_crop_yield_adim16_6, ev_crop_yield_adim16_2, ev_crop_yield_schmidt12_10]. Bunds should not be applied where rainfall is that heavy. The evidence itself names what separates gains from losses. Rainfall: gains concentrate in low-rainfall or variable areas and in drier periods, while bunds lose yield in high-rainfall areas, and in Tigray bunds slightly raised productivity in drier periods but reduced it in moist seasons because cropped area was lost to the bunds [ev_crop_yield_mala24_3, ev_crop_yield_schmidt12_10, ev_crop_yield_schmidt12_8, ev_crop_yield_adim16_6]. Time and maintenance: value of production rose only after structures had been maintained for at least 7 years, later adopters saw no significant gain, and bunds cut yields in the first few years [ev_agricultural_production_value_schmidt12_5, ev_agricultural_production_value_schmidt12_2, ev_crop_yield_adim16_7]. Who decides: imposed structures often reduced cultivable area by 3 to 20% without improving productivity, and structures promoted mostly off-farm for community resource protection gave no gain [ev_crop_yield_roose94_5, ev_crop_yield_abate21_1]. Severity: dry spells can be bridged but yields cannot be sustained in a meteorological drought [ev_crop_yield_rock10_2]. Practice: fanya juu and soil bunds account for the measured losses [ev_crop_yield_adim16_2]. The actionable distinctions are therefore siting by rainfall regime, farmer-owned rather than imposed structures, and a maintenance horizon of years. On quality, many of the largest gains are from bundled programmes or lender completion reports (Ethiopia public works, India watershed projects, Mauritania), with value of production and forage biomass used as proxies, while the losses come from an Ethiopian synthesis and a matched study; the drought finding is a secondary citation in a review [ev_crop_yield_utk22_1, ev_crop_yield_mrt14_2, ev_forage_productivity_mrt14_3, ev_crop_yield_meaza22_1]. The wheat figure is a review's citation of a package that includes biological measures [ev_crop_yield_tade23h1_2]. The nitrogen finding is a content on farm soils, not a yield [ev_soil_nitrogen_sawa11h1_4]. These are compiler and author judgements across groups, direction only, and the review sentence is second-hand; the WOCAT authors also note that some case studies indicate little to no improvement in water use efficiency [ev_rain_water_productivity_faoslm11_1, ev_rain_water_productivity_wocwh13_1, ev_rain_water_productivity_rock10_1].

effect_mechanism: Household income and returns from mixed soil and water conservation and water-harvesting programmes have been found to rise, to stay flat and to fall. Gains run through higher yields, irrigation and diversification: a quasi-experimental study found soil and water conservation raised net rice profit in Ghana by a significant 16 per cent [ev_economic_return_mala24_1]; Brazil's production-cistern programme raised family income by about 4.6%, nearly 11% when the top of the income distribution is excluded, with larger effects on farms of 0 to 10 ha [ev_household_income_casag22_1, ev_household_income_casag22_2, ev_household_income_casag22_5]; a review of 311 Indian watershed case studies found a mean benefit-cost ratio of 2.14 and an internal rate of return of 22 percent [ev_economic_return_josh05_1, ev_economic_return_josh05_2]; Mauritanian dikes returned a financial IRR of 24% [ev_economic_return_mrt14_4]; and programme evaluations report income gains of 54% in Karnataka and 58% on the Loess Plateau over control areas [ev_household_income_iegind11_2, ev_household_income_iegchn07_6]. Losses come from costs exceeding gains: in Burkina Faso the yield increase did not cover the annual costs of single SWC measures [ev_economic_return_zoug14_3]; Ethiopian graded fanya juu and graded soil bunds had net present values of −148 and −708 ETB per hectare [ev_economic_return_adim16_4]; and the Brazilian cistern programme's benefit-cost ratio over its evaluation window was 0.0858 [ev_economic_return_casag22_9].
conditionality: What separates the sides, where the evidence says it: farm size, since the Brazilian income effect was a gain on small farms but a loss on farms larger than 10 ha [ev_household_income_casag22_5, ev_household_income_casag22_6]; labour costing and the size of the initial investment, since Ethiopian household benefit-cost ratios were 0.42 to 0.78 at market wages and exceeded one only with a shadow wage and a low initial investment [ev_economic_return_schmidt12_6]; and how long benefits are counted, since the Brazilian ratio covers a short window against a long-lived asset and counts income only [ev_economic_return_casag22_9]. For a Task Team Leader, the practical points are targeting smallholders, costing household labour honestly and expecting returns to arrive over years. The largest gains are from bundled programmes with weak attribution, and the Brazilian income effects are for a cistern bundled with a productive grant and training [ev_household_income_casag22_1]; IEG calls the China income estimate not robust and notes the India gains may partly be construction wages, and a Karnataka completion report doubts its own before/after figures [ev_household_income_iegchn07_6, ev_household_income_iegind11_2, ev_household_income_kar20_3]. The losses and nulls come mostly from independent evaluations, though the Ethiopian values may omit off-site benefits [ev_economic_return_adim16_4], and a Kenyan bundle showed no effect on per capita income [ev_household_income_mala24_2]. A review's report of increased incomes from check dams and infiltration pits in Malawi is qualitative and cited second-hand [ev_household_income_ngur26_1]. Income and returns are proxies for poverty.

This is not a null finding: studies found real effects, in opposite directions, and the agreement note lists both sides. Read the conditionality for what separates them (transfer: in_context).

effect_mechanism: In the Maghreb, contour structures have been reported both to hold runoff and to accelerate erosion. Staggered earth bunds (tabia) in Morocco store the runoff of all rains below 50 mm on the field [ev_runoff_reduction_roos10_1]. In Algeria, a poorly maintained banquette becomes a factor accelerating erosion, because the smallest unrepaired breach triggers a chain reaction through the whole network in torrential and prolonged rains [ev_erosion_hazard_arab04_2].
conditionality: Two conditions separate the sides in the sources. Maintenance: the acceleration is tied explicitly to unrepaired breaches in state-built banquettes [ev_erosion_hazard_arab04_2]. Storm size: the tabia hold runoff only up to rains of 50 mm, and in bigger storms the excess overtops them and gullies the whole slope [ev_runoff_reduction_roos10_1]. The actionable reading is to plan and fund upkeep and spillways, not only construction. Elsewhere banquettes simply did not stop gullying: gullied areas on Tunisian banquette land grew by 12% between 1963 and 1973, and over 1947-1968 Algerian banquettes had no influence on the sedimentation rate of the Oued Fodda dam [ev_erosion_hazard_arab04_1, ev_sediment_retention_arab04_1]. Neither side is measured on plots: the protective statement is from an expert manual and the harmful ones are secondary citations within a national evaluation, and the two concern different structures, tabia and banquettes [ev_runoff_reduction_roos10_1, ev_erosion_hazard_arab04_2].

justification.statement: water_harvesting_conservation soil_erosion_risk: CONFLICTING EVIDENCE — material weight on both the benefit and the harm side, so no direction is stated. This is not a null finding: studies found real effects, in opposite directions, and the agreement note lists both sides. Read the conditionality for what separates them (transfer: adjacent).

effect_mechanism: In high-income settings check dams and ponds trap sediment: loose-rock check dams on semi-arid USA rangeland watersheds retained 48.4% and 82.4% of total sediment yield and produced a twofold decline in outlet sediment per unit of peak runoff, four field-edge ponds in southern Germany trapped 54-85% of incoming sediment over 8 years, and a typical Belgian pond had a long-term trapping efficiency of 68% [ev_sediment_retention_poly14_1, ev_sediment_retention_poly14_2, ev_sediment_retention_meko14_2, ev_sediment_retention_meko14_3]. Bench terracing in a small USA watershed reduced runoff by 9% and sediment yield by 58% [ev_runoff_reduction_meko14_1].
conditionality: Check dams had no statistically significant effect on the runoff volume of major storms, reducing only the number of runoff events from small storms by 60%, and The twofold decline in outlet sediment was significant only at α = 0.2 [ev_runoff_reduction_poly14_2, ev_runoff_reduction_poly14_1, ev_sediment_retention_poly14_2]. Check dams can also increase erosion downstream: channel incision was observed below 81% of surveyed check dams in a Spanish catchment [ev_erosion_hazard_fran21_1]. Most units are secondary citations in reviews, and the high-income settings (rangeland, arable fields with ponds) differ from smallholder water harvesting [ev_sediment_retention_meko14_2].

effect_mechanism: Physical SWC works under public-works and watershed programmes reduce soil loss and downstream runoff, and sediment-control dams with terraces and vegetation trap sediment in the catchment. A meta-analysis of traditional in-situ water harvesting finds soil loss cut by 58.66% and runoff by 53% on average, with soil and stone bunds reducing soil loss by 55.06% and runoff by 49.2% [ev_erosion_hazard_tefe24_1, ev_runoff_reduction_tefe24_1, ev_erosion_hazard_tefe24_4, ev_runoff_reduction_tefe24_5]; in Ethiopian catchments, stone bunds, check dams and vegetation regrowth cut sediment yield from 8.5 to 1.9 t per hectare a year [ev_erosion_hazard_meko14_1, ev_erosion_hazard_meko14_2].
conditionality: Nearly all units are programme or lender reports from Ethiopia, India and China, often perception surveys or before/after comparisons; an Uttarakhand water budget showed surface runoff slightly increasing, the Karnataka runoff comparison is against another SWC programme, and IEG doubts the India runoff measurements. Effects mixing runoff and soil-loss metrics are only components of erosion risk. A catchment-restoration meta-analysis in Ethiopia finds minimal effect of catchment treatment on runoff in drought-prone areas with annual rainfall below 500 mm [ev_runoff_reduction_meaza22_3]. The Ethiopian catchment results combine structures with grazing control and vegetation regeneration and are cited in a review, so the share due to the works is not isolated [ev_erosion_hazard_meko14_1].

effect_mechanism: Storage and recharge structures ease water stress in semi-arid areas: production cisterns in semi-arid Brazil keep livestock watered while clay tanks are dry, an agency review credits consumption and production cisterns with a large drop in rural establishments without any water source, and subsurface dams raise water levels in existing wells used when other sources dry up [ev_water_access_deficit_arsky20_5, ev_water_access_deficit_castro22_1, ev_water_access_deficit_cirilo03_1]. In the field, pits and furrows keep rain in the root zone: in Burkina Faso zaï of 30–40 cm diameter and 1-m half-moons retained moisture for 2-3 weeks through dry spells, and zaï can retain moisture in the soil for seven to ten days after rainfall; in semi-arid Brazil tied furrows kept more soil moisture than the traditional flat system at all crop stages and depths [ev_soil_water_retention_zour25h1_7, ev_soil_water_retention_sawa11h1_8, ev_soil_water_retention_brito07_9].
conditionality: Supply is bounded by storage: 57% of Kenyan sand dams would hold 4 months of water for their reported beneficiaries [ev_water_access_deficit_neuf17_1]. The Brazilian units are implementer or agency assessments, interviews or census inference from an upper-middle-income context rather than the low-income target [ev_water_access_deficit_castro22_1, ev_water_access_deficit_arsky20_5]. Well-level evidence for semi-arid bunds and zaï now sits in the catchment water yield rows. What upstream capture does to water downstream is a separate question, answered in the catchment water yield rows. The zaï and half-moon results come with compost in the pits, so the moisture gain cannot be credited to the pit alone [ev_soil_water_retention_zour25h1_7, ev_soil_water_retention_sawa11h1_8]. In the Brazilian trial deep ploughing, which is tillage alone and not a capture structure, scored as high as the tied furrows, and the trial ran a single season at a station of the agency that promotes the technology [ev_soil_water_retention_brito07_9].

effect_mechanism: Terraces and check dams hold water where it is needed. A global terracing synthesis finds terraced sites more efficient than slopes at reducing runoff and conserving soil water (e.g., soil moisture recharge), with a mean δsm of 1.2 [ev_soil_water_retention_wei16_1], and a check-dam review reports that check dams that store seasonal runoff solve local scarcity in supply [ev_water_access_deficit_luca21_1].
conditionality: Both sources pool cases from high- and lower-income countries, so the cell does not isolate the low-income target [ev_soil_water_retention_wei16_1, ev_water_access_deficit_luca21_1]. The terracing ratio is an unweighted mean across extracted cases, and soil moisture is read as a component of water stress rather than water stress itself [ev_soil_water_retention_wei16_1]. The check-dam finding is a secondary citation within the review [ev_water_access_deficit_luca21_1]. What upstream capture does to water downstream is answered in the catchment water yield rows.

effect_mechanism: Watershed treatment reduces reliance on outside supply: participating villages in India saw reduced water transportation by tanker compared with nonparticipating villages [ev_water_access_deficit_verm19_1], and an agency review credits consumption and production cisterns in semi-arid Brazil with a significant contribution to wider access to water [ev_water_access_deficit_castro22_1]. In India, discharge of springs and streams rose in treated watersheds: a sample study in Himachal Pradesh reports a 40 percent increase in water discharge in spring and stream sources [ev_water_regulation_hp17_1], and the Uttarakhand project achieved an average 21 percent increase in water discharge from perennial water sources in sampled micro-watersheds, against a target of 25 percent [ev_water_regulation_utk22_6]. Measured soil moisture adds a field route: a meta-analysis of in-situ practices finds they improve soil moisture retention by 59%, with soil/stone bunds at an SMD of 76.4% [ev_soil_water_retention_tefe24_1, ev_soil_water_retention_tefe24_3]; in Burkina Faso zaï of 30–40 cm diameter and 1-m half-moons retained moisture for 2-3 weeks through dry spells [ev_soil_water_retention_zour25h1_7]; and Indian project watersheds showed an increase in soil moisture content by 30.5 percent compared to the IWMP sites [ev_soil_water_retention_kar20_2]. Water productivity, the grain produced per unit of rain, is a route by which capture eases water stress. The water-productivity evidence points the same way: FAO compilers list improved water use efficiency among the main benefits of rainwater harvesting, the WOCAT guideline authors find that all water harvesting groups indicate improved water use efficiency, mostly high to medium, through reduced evaporation loss and better soil water availability, and a review sentence, citing earlier work, says capture approaches often lead also to higher water productivity because denser canopies shade the soil [ev_rain_water_productivity_faoslm11_1, ev_rain_water_productivity_wocwh13_1, ev_rain_water_productivity_rock10_1].
conditionality: The tanker reduction is a reported programme assessment [ev_water_access_deficit_verm19_1], and the Brazilian unit is an agency inference from census figures in an upper-middle-income context [ev_water_access_deficit_castro22_1]. The Indian spring and stream discharge figures come from World Bank completion reports, the lender's own evaluation, measured before and after without untreated comparison sites, for catchment treatment that bundles plantations, trenches, ponds and check dams with water-harvesting structures, so the gain cannot be credited to water harvesting alone [ev_water_regulation_hp17_1, ev_water_regulation_utk22_6]. Groundwater-recharge evidence, with its limits, now sits in the catchment water yield rows, which also answer what upstream capture does to water downstream. The pooled 59% covers mixed in-situ practices, and the zaï and half-moon result comes with compost in the pits, so neither credits a single structure [ev_soil_water_retention_tefe24_1, ev_soil_water_retention_zour25h1_7]. The Indian soil-moisture comparison is a project-commissioned study of a package of soil and water conservation structures [ev_soil_water_retention_kar20_2]. These are compiler and author judgements across groups, direction only, and the review sentence is second-hand; the WOCAT authors also note that some case studies indicate little to no improvement in water use efficiency [ev_rain_water_productivity_faoslm11_1, ev_rain_water_productivity_wocwh13_1, ev_rain_water_productivity_rock10_1].
